data.cultural_impact: Johanna is a popular name in various Christian cultures. In the Catholic tradition, there is a well-known saint named Saint Joan of Arc, who was a fifteenth-century French warrior and visionary. She heard voices from saints urging her to help France, and she played a significant role in securing victory for the French during the Hundred Years War. The name Johanna is closely associated with her legacy, as she was also known as Jeanne or Joan the Maid.

biblical_reference.note: Johanna is mentioned in the New Testament as a follower of Jesus Christ and a helper of the apostles.

historical_references.reference: In the Middle Ages, Johanna was a popular name for Jewish girls who were converted to Christianity. One famous example is Johanna of Arc (1412-1431), who was born Joan of Arc, but took the name Johanna when she was canonized in 1456.

Another historical reference for the name Johanna comes from the New Testament, where it is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Hannah. Hannah is the mother of the prophet Samuel, and her story is told in the Old Testament book of 1 Samuel.
